title: Climate Change and Sustainability

standard_text: Impacts of climate change on people and ecosystems; mitigation and adaptation; global and local sustainability. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 3, theme: Science and Development)
meta_desc: Free JSS 3 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Science and Development): evidence and indicators, climate models and predictions, impacts on people and ecosystems, carbon footprints and sources and mitigation and adaptation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Rising CO₂ and temperatures change ecosystems, oceans and communities.
key_sub: Mitigation reduces emissions; adaptation reduces harm.
body_html:
How to think about it

Evidence of climate change includes higher average temperatures, rising CO₂ (now more than 420 ppm), shrinking glaciers and sea ice, rising sea level and ocean acidification. Ice cores and tree rings show how the climate changed in the past.

In Nigeria, impacts include desertification in the north, the shrinking of Lake Chad, heavier floods, and sea-level rise along the coast near Lagos. Mitigation cuts emissions (renewable energy, public transport, efficient buildings); adaptation prepares for change (sea walls, mangrove planting, early warning systems, drought-tolerant rice).

Example

CO₂ rose from 340 ppm in 1980 to 420 ppm in 2020. Average rise per year?

80 ppm ÷ 40 years

Answer: 2 ppm per year

Example

Is building a sea wall mitigation or adaptation?

It protects against the effect, not the cause.

Answer: adaptation

Common mistakes

  • Thinking one cool month disproves climate change.
  • Saying melting sea ice is the main cause of sea-level rise: melting land ice and warming water are.
  • Mixing up mitigation and adaptation.

faq.q: Why does sea level rise as the ocean warms?
faq.a: Water expands when it warms, and melting land ice adds more water.
The fall in ocean pH as sea water absorbs extra CO₂, which makes it harder for shellfish and corals to build shells.
